## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sutanujātaka* (Ja 398) is a canonical birth tale in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to its nidāna framework, the Buddha recounted this story while dwelling at Jetavana regarding a monk who dutifully supported his mother, an introductory circumstance noted as recurring in the Sāma Birth (*Sāmajātaka*) [SuttaCentral]. In the story's index entry, the titular protagonist Sutanu (or Sutano), a young man (*māṇava*) born into a poor householder's family (*duggata-gahapatiputta*), is identified as the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1897]. Later Ceylonese historical tradition records the prominence of the text: according to the *Cūḷavaṁsa*, the *Sutanujātaka* was one of thirty-two selected birth tales depicted in coloured paintings on the walls of a courtyard [Geiger 1953].
In terms of text reuse and textual parallels, text-matching data from DharmaNexus identifies twelve shared passages between this canonical text and the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0513a3), with the longest continuous correspondence running between segments §1.4–4.4 and §2953–2964 of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any external cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral notes four modern translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral].
